messages.subject: Information about the 3v Wallace and changeRangeR package, to calculate the representativeness
parts:
Hello

i Would like to know how could get the v.3 Wallace, in particular i'm interested to use the package changerangeR. For my studies i would need  to calculate the protected areas representativeness of species' areal.

Kind regards.

messages.author: 881c0dd9c7b0d196
messages.subject: Re: Information about the 3v Wallace and changeRangeR package, to calculate the representativeness
parts:
Currently (and only temporarily), changeRangeR is off CRAN so it will need to be installed via github:

library(devtools)
devtools::install_github("https://github.com/wallaceEcoMod/changeRangeR")
library(changeRangeR)

For information, see the publication. changeRangeR also has two vignettes that may be helpful.
Single Species Analyses: https://wallaceEcoMod.github.io/changeRangeR/singleSpeciesMetrics.html 
Biodiversity Metrics: https://wallaceEcoMod.github.io/changeRangeR/BiodivMetrics.html 

changeRangeR is also available within the developmental version of wallace ("v3"). This can also be installed via github. Keep in mind, this is a developmental version as we continue to improve its functionality. You may need to install the archives of the `rgeos`, `rgdal`, and `maptools` packages to get v3 to work, as we are in progress in removing these expired packages.

library(devtools)
devtools::install_github("https://github.com/wallaceEcoMod/wallace/tree/biomodelos")

messages.subject: Re: Messaggio privato su: Information about the 3v Wallace and changeRangeR package, to calculate the representativeness
parts:
Your raster files can be saved anywhere on your machine, you just need to edit the code to use the correct path.

p<- raster("put/your/path/here/and/make/sure/it/ends/with/.tif") 

On a Windows machine, Shift + Right click will bring up the option to "copy as path" that you can paste in the code to get the path to the file.
